clue.text: Animal turned up with mother

indicators.note: turned means the little word up is flipped round and read the other way

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A creature rolls over beside its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads naturally as one phrase, but 'turned' alone is the reversal signal and 'up' is the word reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma is a large wild cat of the Americas, an example of an animal.

clue.text: One who oversees meeting with Chinese pilot

parts.note: an airman is a pilot or member of an air force

explanation.surface: Someone running a meeting with a pilot from China.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman is the person who presides over a meeting or committee, keeping it in order.

clue.text: Spool for thread endlessly going up and down

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for going up and down loses its final letter

parts.note: bobbing is moving up and down, like a float on water

explanation.surface: A cotton reel that keeps rising and falling without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the G from BOBBING.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is a small cylinder on which thread is wound in a sewing machine or loom.

clue.text: See 12 across
In a rush to charge queen

parts.note: a person in your charge is in your care
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying to accuse the queen of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' means custody here, not an accusation or a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle or speed along headlong, so it is a verb meaning to hurry.

clue.text: End of scarf covered by moist part of cloth

indicators.note: covered by means the letter picked goes inside the word for moist

parts.note: wet means moist or damp

indicators.note: End of means the last letter of scarf is taken

explanation.surface: A damp scarf whose end is part of the fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' takes F from scarf; 'covered by' puts it within WET.
explanation.definitionFit: The weft is the set of crosswise threads woven through the warp in a fabric.

clue.text: Chef covering up hot item used for kitchen storage

indicators.note: covering means the word for chef wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a chef is a cook
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cook putting a lid over a hot dish in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is the containment signal; 'up' is taken literally rather than as a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup hook is a small screw-in hook under a shelf on which mugs and cups are hung.

clue.text: Party attended by composer leaving new widow

indicators.note: attended by means the party word comes first with the rest following it

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for new is removed from the composer

parts.note: Richard Wagner was a German composer

explanation.surface: A gathering visited by a composer who walks out on a new widow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' looks like the composer walking out, but it removes the N for 'new' from his name; 'attended by' puts the party first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow who holds a title or property from her late husband.

clue.text: Country involved in formal investigation

indicators.note: involved in means the answer sits inside the run of letters across formal investigation

explanation.surface: A nation caught up in an official inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' signals the letters at the join of forMAL Investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Schubert composition about a European capital

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters surround the little word a
a composition is an arrangement, so the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Schubert piece written about a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' turns SCHUBERT into BUCHREST, and 'about' wraps it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania, an example of a European capital.

clue.text: Fish go into chippy

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to go into

explanation.surface: A fish is dropped into the fryer at a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippy' looks like a chip shop (British slang), but it is also British slang for a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is informal British slang for a woodworker, from the chips of wood they make.

clue.text: Film-maker in scruffy anorak limps on

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy, so the letters of the phrase are messed up

explanation.surface: A director in a shabby coat hobbling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' rearranges ANORAK LIMPS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman Polanski is the Polish-French director of films such as Chinatown and Rosemary's Baby.

clue.text: Type of race put down again

definitions.meaning: a team race with runners taking turns
to ... is to lay something, such as a carpet, a second time

explanation.surface: A kind of race, or setting something down once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a team race in legs, and re-lay means lay again, as with flooring.

clue.text: Check design of trainers

indicators.note: a design is a fresh arrangement, so the letters of trainers are rearranged

explanation.surface: Inspecting how a pair of trainers is designed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design of' rearranges TRAINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, the same as keeping it under control.

clue.text: Aides trained to make plans

indicators.note: trained means taught or shaped, so the letters of aides are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Assistants given training so they can draw up plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges AIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are plans or schemes that someone has thought up.

clue.text: Eagle never crossing valley

indicators.note: crossing means the answer straddles the gap between Eagle and never

explanation.surface: An eagle that never flies across the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' signals the letters across eaGLE Never.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Country losing territory on North Island to old Britons

indicators.note: on means the remaining letters come before the following pieces
losing means the word for territory is taken off the country

parts.note: Iceland is a country in the North Atlantic
land is territory
I is the abbreviation for Island, as on maps

explanation.surface: A nation giving up ground on a northern island to the ancient British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes LAND from ICELAND, leaving ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe of East Anglia led by Boudicca against Rome.

clue.text: Independent publications losing Azerbaijani leaders' pictures

indicators.note: losing means the leading letters of the Azerbaijani word are removed from the publications

parts.note: magazines are periodical publications

indicators.note: leaders' means the opening letters of Azerbaijani are taken

explanation.surface: Independent magazines dropping images of Azerbaijan's leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders'' gives AZ, the first two letters of Azerbaijani, and 'losing' takes AZ from MAGAZINES, leaving MAGINES.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form an image of it in the mind, so pictures matches the verb.

clue.text: One attempting to lose runs level

indicators.note: to lose means the abbreviation for runs is dropped from the word for someone attempting

parts.note: a trier is one who tries or attempts
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps trying stops scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' drops one R from TRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or layer, such as one level of seating in a stadium.

clue.text: Experiment involving long container

indicators.note: involving means the word for experiment contains the other piece

parts.note: a test is an experiment or trial
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A long-running trial taking place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective about the experiment, but it is a verb meaning yearn; 'involving' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden box, originally for shipping tea, often used in house moves.

clue.text: Strangely tasty cep seen as belonging to the same sort

definitions.text: seen as belonging to the same sort

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mushroom that tastes odd but is regarded as one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges TASTY CEP; a cep is a porcini mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor typecast is always given the same type of role, regarded as only fit for one kind.

clue.text: Space given to lean recruit

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
to list is to lean, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A thin new recruit given some room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' looks like an adjective (thin), but it is a verb meaning tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign someone up for service, the same as signing up new members.

clue.text: Set of clubs given to girl

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl being handed a set of golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set of clubs' reads as golf gear, but 'Set' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a set or group of things or people sharing some quality.

clue.text: Social 20 across accepting large, grand residence

indicators.note: accepting means the social group takes in the abbreviation for large

parts.note: 20 across is class, and a social class is a caste
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A class of society welcoming in a big, grand home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts L within CASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a large fortified building, the stately home of a lord or monarch.

clue.text: Game played by poets nursing sick setter

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the poets wrap round the other pieces

parts.note: bards are poets
ill means sick
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Poets playing a game while looking after an ailing crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' means holding, not caring for the sick, so it signals containment; the setter is I by convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue sport played on a cloth-covered table with balls and pockets.

clue.text: Hit boy below the belt

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for boy, as in birth notices
low means unfair

explanation.surface: Striking a lad with an unfair punch below the belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below the belt' means unfair, hence LOW, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a hit or punch, the noun for a strike.

clue.text: Bird that can cough things up?

definitions.meaning: to clear the throat noisily, bringing up phlegm

explanation.surface: A bird that brings up what it has eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawk names a raptor, and as a verb means to clear the throat by coughing up phlegm.

clue.text: Bird heard when crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the sound-alike letters go across the river abbreviation
heard means the word when is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: when, said aloud, sounds just like wen with the h unheard

explanation.surface: A bird is heard as it flies over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns WHEN into WEN by sound, and 'crossing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wren is a tiny brown songbird with a cocked tail.

clue.text: Vagrant stealing first part of investigator's brief

indicators.note: stealing means the vagrant takes in the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough

indicators.note: first part of means the opening letter of investigator's is taken

explanation.surface: A tramp pinches part of a detective's case notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first part of' gives I; 'stealing' puts it within DOSSER (British slang for a rough sleeper).
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is a set of papers on a case, the same as a file of documents about it.

clue.text: Sticky stuff coating large end of rectangular dressing

indicators.note: coating means the sticky stuff wraps round the letter for large

parts.note: paste is sticky stuff, like glue

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of rectangular is taken

explanation.surface: Adhesive on a large rectangular dressing for a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' puts L inside PASTE, and 'end of' adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking plaster is a dressing or adhesive bandage put over a small wound.
